marketInsightsHtml: Une pression haussière supplémentaire émerge du marché français, où les travailleurs d'EDF doivent entamer une grève de 24 heures ce soir à 21 heures. Le potentiel de réduction de la production nucléaire s’ajoute aux inquiétudes existantes concernant la disponibilité de la production française, avec une proportion importante du parc déjà hors service pour maintenance.

marketInsights.gas: European gas prices are trading higher this morning as the market continues hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough between the US and Iran fade. The TTF front month contract has opened around 92.35 €/MWh, 0.50 €/MWh higher day on day. Yesterday's heavy sell-off, driven by reports that a draft memorandum of understanding had been approved by Washington, with both sides reportedly making concessions over Iran's nuclear programme, quickly lost momentum after Tehran rejected suggestions that an agreement was close. Sentiment has since become increasingly bullish following renewed disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, with reports overnight claiming as many as four tankers had caught fire after striking naval mines. The US midterm elections have added another layer of uncertainty, with Democratic gains in Congress potentially limiting Trump's ability to pursue his foreign policy agenda, although the new Congress will not take office until January. European supply fundamentals remain relatively tight, with colder weather and unplanned outages across Norwegian gas infrastructure continuing to restrict available export capacity. European storage also remain low, sitting at 74% full at time of writing, leaving the market more exposed to supply disruptions and any sustained increase in winter demand.
marketInsights.power: European power prices moved lower yesterday, tracking the sharp losses across gas markets as optimism surrounding a potential US-Iran agreement weighed on energy markets. However, the credibility of those reports came into question with Iran rejecting claims a deal with the US was close. Since then the market has retraced those losses with the German Baseload front month contract pricing at 206.50 €/MWh at open this morning, up 1.90 €/MWh day on day. Power is also being supported by weather, with cooler forecasts for week 47 expected to lift heating demand, while subdued wind generation is likely to increase reliance on gas for power generation. Additional upside pressure is emerging from the French market, where EDF workers are due to begin a 24-hour strike at 9pm this evening. The potential for reduced nuclear output adds to existing concerns over French generation availability, with a significant proportion of the fleet already offline for maintenance.
